title: Uniform Dosage Optimality for K-Way Interaction Estimation under Shared Supply Limits
banked_reason: The main delivered result is exact population A-optimality in a narrow fixed-dimensional product-Bernoulli model, not finite-sample optimal-design or minimax optimality; D0.5.G capped it at incremental with paper-score ceiling 6.4 below the 7.4 field cutoff.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and panel-checked the exact shared-supply population optimizer, stability certificate, leverage and rank obstruction, and a fixed-threshold O(n^-1) oracle-risk expansion; the math panel reported no findings and the cited sources were verified. The package collapsed only at the field-novelty gate: it remains a narrow fixed-dimensional specialization, while the tier-moving finite-sample dosage/minimax frontier is unproved and explicitly outside scope.
tldr: For independent product-Bernoulli assignment and the fixed complete Fourier basis through order \(k\), the population \(A\)-criterion is an explicit elementary-symmetric polynomial. Its unique shared-supply optimizer is the uniform dosage \(u=\min\{L/p,1/2\}\), with an exact criterion value and a global quadratic stability certificate whose coefficient is sharp when \(L\ge p/2\). Exact leverage and a rare-activation rank obstruction complement a two-sided threshold-OLS risk theorem. A fixed spectral threshold, the mean-zero whitened Gram, and a second-order inverse identity yield an explicit uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) relative-risk expansion at fixed dimension. This is oracle attainment at the population-optimal independent design, not finite-sample dosage minimaxity.
gap: The modern PFED paper resolves limited supply analytically only for additive responses and reports numerical evidence for interaction models. Classical product-design theory gives the inverse-trace identity but not the shared expected-supply optimizer or the stated risk translation.
fill: The project derives the exact all-order criterion, proves uniform dosage with a sharp global modulus, and couples it to exact leverage, rank-failure probability, and unconditional threshold-OLS risk.
